    {"name": "resolution_hours", "analytical_usefulness": 0.95, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Directly the target quantity (time to resolve), derivable from opened_at and closed_at. This is the core outcome variable for the query. NULLs correspond to open/unclosed incidents, which is correct behaviour."},
    {"name": "priority_score", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Numeric encoding of the existing priority column; useful as a modeling/grouping signal for resolution time, though largely redundant with the original priority field. Values are grounded in that column."},
    {"name": "category_avg_resolution_hours", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Category-level mean resolution time gives a genuine grouping signal (some categories resolve slower). Derived aggregate from in-table data, though it leaks the target and is per-category constant."},
    {"name": "assignee_avg_resolution_hours", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Assignee historical average resolution time is a plausible predictive signal for slow resolution and is derivable by aggregating over assigned_to. Reasonable target-encoding style feature."},
    {"name": "group_avg_resolution_hours", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Assignment-group average resolution time; a legitimate new axis to compare which teams are slower. Grounded aggregate over assignment_group."},
    {"name": "opened_hour_of_day", "analytical_usefulness": 0.65, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Extracted hour from opened_at; a plausible temporal signal for resolution delay. Values are a sound reading of the timestamp."},
    {"name": "is_afterhours_open", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "After-hours flag is a reasonable, non-constant signal potentially correlated with slower resolution; derivable from opened_at hour."},
    {"name": "is_weekend_open", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Weekend-open flag is a sensible signal for delayed resolution and is directly derivable from the opened date."},
    {"name": "description_length", "analytical_usefulness": 0.3, "source_groundedness": 0.95, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Raw character length of short_description is a generic surface feature with weak analytical leverage for this query, though trivially grounded in the text."},
    {"name": "is_unassigned", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Unassigned flag is a meaningful, non-constant signal—unassigned tickets plausibly linger longer. Derivable from assigned_to being empty."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.72,
  "source_groundedness": 0.88,
  "rationale": "Most added columns give genuine axes (resolution time, priority, category/assignee/group historical averages, temporal and assignment flags) directly relevant to why an incident resolves slowly, and their values are soundly derivable from in-table timestamps and categorical fields. Weaker points: priority_score is largely redundant with the original priority column, and description_length is a generic surface feature with little leverage for this query. No hallucinations observed in the samples; NULL resolution_hours for open incidents is correct behaviour."
}
